findings.title: Empty update data throws and doesn't bump updatedAt
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with empty data. Prisma updateMany rejects empty data with a validation error, so this line will throw and break cache warm-up. Even if it did not throw, updateMany does not auto-touch @updatedAt, so an empty update would never change updatedAt. Pass an explicit timestamp like { updatedAt: new Date() }.

findings.title: Delete-cache success never refreshes cache status
findings.body: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only shows a toast and calls onSuccess?.(). Unlike disconnectMutation it never invalidates trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, so after deleting the cache the dropdown still shows the old cacheUpdatedAt until a full page reload. Invalidate the connectedCalendars query on settle/success.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired rows
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows by credentialId with no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only honors rows with expiresAt >= now. The UI will therefore show Last updated for credentials whose cache is entirely expired and unusable. Add the same expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } filter.

findings.title: Unfiltered credentialIds passed to cache query
findings.body: credentialIds is built as connectedCalendars.map((cal) => cal.credentialId) with no filtering/dedup. If the list is empty or contains null/undefined (e.g. delegation-credential entries without a DB credentialId), prisma.calendarCache.groupBy with credentialId: { in: [...] } receives invalid values and throws, failing the whole connectedCalendars query. Filter to finite numbers and dedupe before calling.

findings.title: Helper script is macOS-only and writes wrong .env
findings.body: ENV_FILE is set to ../.env so running the script from the repo root edits the parent directory instead of the repo .env, and sed -i '' -E is BSD/macOS syntax that fails on GNU/Linux. The script also silently rewrites GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in the env file. Fix the path resolution and make the sed invocation portable or document it as macOS-only.
